claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the trace, not the receipt's rounded copy: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events is 18.0 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 8.0 km or 80% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%) and clears the 50% limb as well, which is why the derived deviation status is 'material'. The trip record's own 18.0 km agrees with the trace figure, so the trace-governs sentence in POL-RD-01 raises no conflict here and no discount for a rounded convenience copy is available to the driver.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on cited artifacts: the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip id TRP-09113, and the trace's first fix at 2026-09-20T18:20:00 matches the trip record's started_at and the fare breakdown's trip window. The excess is measured from an unimpaired trace that the admissibility pre-pass assessed COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with zero gaps, so limb (b) is satisfied directly and no independent source is needed. The rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 never engages. The burden has therefore shifted to the driver to name a specific artifact and clause.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the driver cannot route this case to a 'no corroboration' outcome: POL-RD-07 limb (a) requires a gap over 90 seconds between consecutive fixes, limb (b) a straight-line jump over 500 m, limb (c) a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace has 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the limbs fires, so the deviation stands on the trace alone.

Even taking the driver's closure defence at its highest under POL-RD-03, the exoneration is capped and the cap bites hard. The advisory ADV-20260920-113 is a CLOSURE on the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, active 18:14 to 18:55 and overlapping the trip window 18:20 to 18:54, and the booked optimal route is recorded as running via that same named segment, so limb (a) and limb (b) are met. But the justified excess is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00), which is min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = min(8.0, 3.60) = 3.60 km. At most 3.60 km of the 8.0 km excess is exonerated. The remaining 4.40 km is beyond the cap, is not exonerated on any reading, and is refundable under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route.

The closure-adjusted optimal route that POL-RD-03 requires is 13.60 km: booked optimal 10.0 km plus the justified excess of 3.60 km. Its duration is the booked 20.0 minutes scaled by the ratio of adjusted to booked distance, 20.0 x (13.60 / 10.0) = 27.2 minutes. The trip record's amended_optimal_duration_min is null, so the scaled figure governs and no stored alternative displaces it.

The refund is arithmetic. The fare model on this trip is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs and no upfront-quote bar under POL-RD-11 applies. The surge multiplier is read from the fare_breakdown artifact EV-FARE-09113's surge_multiplier field and is 1.0. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route + 0.00 waiting_time_fee - 0.00 promo_discount = 23.416. charged_total is 31.42. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested amount in full.

The off-route ERP must not be counted twice. The Industrial loop exit gantry charged at SGD 2.80 is flagged on_optimal_route false and its nearest trace fix is 223.17 m, so it is a genuine crossing on the deviating stretch; under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the SGD 8.05 recomputation, because the recomputed fare includes only the on-optimal-route Pelton line. It should be itemised in the ruling for transparency and must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

Separately from the distance refund, the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' line is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The line carries coordinates (lat 1.33, lng 103.883), so the match is decidable, and the rule treats only a fix within 250 m of the gantry as a crossing. The nearest trace fix to that gantry is 834.18 m away, at fix index 13, timestamped 18:22:10; the trace never comes close to it. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists, and because the only unmatched line in the fare breakdown is the one refunded under this limb, POL-RD-10(8) is expressly not triggered. This SGD 1.00 is independent of the SGD 8.05 POL-RD-02 figure and is not netted against it.

The driver cannot move the 4.40 km of uncapped excess onto the rider as a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. The rider's only message is 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion', which comes from the rider and is timestamped 18:23:10, but limb (c) requires the instruction to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on, and both chat messages carry waypoint_hint null. Where waypoint_hint is null and no road is named, the corroboration test is undecidable on the record: in the words of the clause, it cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and no excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor may be excluded as rider-requested. Consent to 'the lawful diversion' is consent to the lawful alternative the advisory describes, not to an 18.0 km route.

I do not overstate the repeat-conduct limb: the material deviation does require the driver_profile check under POL-RD-06, and the rider does not claim an uplift on this record. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, which is neither 3 or more flags nor a ratio of 0.05 or more, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) follows and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available. The rider's remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial computed above.

Profile fields that the clauses do not name cannot carry any finding against either party. The rider's prior_no_show_flags (1), prior_disputes_filed (1) and prior_disputes_upheld (0), and the driver's prior_deviation_flags (0), lifetime_trips, rating and acceptance_rate, are context only under POL-GEN-01; the lifetime counters are near-synonyms of, and not substitutes for, the trailing-window counters the clauses actually name, and nothing on either profile may be used to establish a fact about this trip.

This case should be ruled, not escalated. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires: the trip identifiers on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown all read TRP-09113; the trace is unimpaired so trigger (3) is out; the pickup time 18:20:00 is consistent across artifacts and no timestamp runs backwards; the exculpatory clause the driver relies on, POL-RD-03, is supported by an advisory actually present in the pool and covering the trip window; the computed refund is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total; the evidence is not evenly balanced, because the driver's best case is capped at 3.60 km against a measured 8.0 km; and the only unmatched charge line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. A monetary ruling should issue.

NO_ACTION is party-relative and on this record would leave the rider carrying the whole unjustified excess. The rider filed this dispute, the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so declining to act would simply preserve the SGD 8.05 the rider is contesting. What the evidence supports is the return of that contested amount as a PARTIAL_REFUND, with the SGD 1.00 billing-integrity correction standing independently alongside it.

claims.text: The LTA advisory ADV-20260920-113 on EV-ADVIS-09113-01 is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE of the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, active 18:14-18:55 on 2026-09-20, which brackets the 18:20-18:54 trip window with the 15-minute buffer at each end. The platform's own optimal route runs through that very segment - the trip record's optimal_route_source reads 'routing-engine-v3.2 snapshot 2026-09-20 18:12 SGT via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory' - so limbs (a) and (b) of POL-RD-03 are met. Limb (c) is met too: the driver reported at 18:22:40 that the closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, the fare_breakdown charges the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry at 18:42, and the trace shows a route that left the Pelton Canal Link corridor and rejoined it past the closed segment. The closure does not merely 'explain' this diversion; it exonerates the driving it forced.

That exoneration is capped, and the cap on this trip is 3.60 km: min(measured excess 8.0 km, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km 12.0 - optimal_distance_km 10.0) + 1.00) = min(8.0, 3.60). The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 10.0 + 3.60 = 13.60 km, and its derived duration is optimal_duration_min 20.0 scaled by (13.60 / 10.0) = 27.2 minutes, rounded to one decimal place; amended_optimal_duration_min is null on EV-TRIP-09113, so the scaled figure governs and no substitute may be invented. Every downstream number - the POL-RD-01 establishment test and the POL-RD-02 recomputation alike - has to be run on 13.60 km and 27.2 minutes, not on the booked 10.0 km and 20.0 minutes.

The departure from the optimal corridor was rider-directed, not the driver's unilateral choice. At 18:22:40 the driver told the rider the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop; at 18:23:10 the rider answered 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion.' That is a rider instruction under POL-RD-04(a), and it falls within limb (b): the diversion entry gantry is not charged until 18:29, so the instruction precedes the corridor exit. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so I do not pretend the waypoint limb of (c) can be run; the clause's alternative limb - that the vehicle travels the requested road - is satisfied, because the fare_breakdown charges the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry and the trace comes within 223.17 m of it, placing the vehicle on the industrial loop the rider authorised. The excess attributable to that rider-directed diversion is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

On the arithmetic the driver's exposure is bounded, and the ruling must not exceed it. Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal, with the surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown (surge_multiplier 1.0 on EV-FARE-09113): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 of ERP on the optimal route = 23.416; charged_total is 31.42; refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 8.05. Run the identical arithmetic on the booked 10.0 km / 20.0 min baseline and the refund would be 12.75 - which would charge this driver for the very closure POL-RD-03 excuses him for. The lower figure is the correct one, and it is the ceiling.

The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry, which carries on_optimal_route false on EV-FARE-09113, must not be refunded twice. POL-RD-09(1) makes off-route ERP already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, precisely because the recomputed fare counts only gantries lying on the optimal route - here the Pelton lawful diversion entry at 1.00. The off-route line may be itemised in the ruling for transparency, but adding it on top of the POL-RD-02 figure would pay the same 2.80 a second time.

No billing-integrity refund arises on that off-route line either. The 'Industrial loop exit' gantry at 1.338, 103.897 is matched to the trace: the nearest fix is 223.17 m away, inside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) prescribes, so the line records a crossing the vehicle actually made and is not a phantom charge against a gantry the trace never passes.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so no uplift and no referral follows. POL-RD-06's test runs on two fields only, and both are clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 610, so neither limb - 3 or more flags, or a flag rate of 0.05 or more over at least 40 completed trips - is met. No FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is available, and POL-GEN-01 confines the test to those trailing-window counters.

After the POL-RD-03 adjustment the excess remaining is 4.4 km (18.0 - 13.60). That is 32.4% of the 13.60 km adjusted optimal and below the 8.0 km absolute mark, so the deviation is established but not MATERIAL under POL-RD-01; and even measured against the unadjusted 10.0 km baseline it is 44%, still under the 50% materiality line. The material limb of POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged on this trip, and the most this record supports is a POL-RD-02 partial refund, never a full one.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, here is the decision.

1) A diversion happened, and the trace is what measures it. The GPS trace EV-GPS-09113 runs 18.0 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 10.0 km on EV-TRIP-09113 - an excess of 8.0 km, or 80%, past both POL-RD-01 gates (>20% and >0.8 km) and initially material. The trace governs over the trip record's rounded copy, though here they agree. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 205 fixes at 10-second spacing, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 seconds, empty gaps array - so POL-RD-07 gives no ground to discount it and no independent corroboration is needed.

2) The closure excuses part of that excess, but only the capped part. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 closes the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector - the very segment the platform's booked optimal route uses - and its window covers the trip, so POL-RD-03 limbs (a) and (b) are met and limb (c) is corroborated by the route leaving the Pelton corridor and rejoining it. The justified excess is capped at min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 13.60 km, and its duration is 20.0 x (13.60/10.0) = 27.2 minutes (amended_optimal_duration_min is null, so the scaled figure governs). The excess left over is 4.40 km (18.0 - 13.60): still established, but no longer material once the closure adjustment is made.

3) The driver's rider-requested-detour defence (POL-RD-04) does not run. The rider's message 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion' comes from the rider and is in time, but it names no road, and both chat messages carry waypoint_hint null. The clause's corroboration test therefore cannot be run - the clause says so itself - the clause is unavailable, and none of the 4.40 km is excluded as rider-directed. So the driver's claim that the whole departure was rider-authorised is rejected.

4) The refund is arithmetic, not discretion. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-09113), so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not apply, and the surge multiplier is read from EV-FARE-09113's surge_multiplier field as 1.00. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.00) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP = 23.416. charged_total = 31.42. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05.

5) ERP: two charge lines, two different answers. The SGD 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' line is a genuine off-route crossing - the nearest fix is 223.17 m, inside the 250 m radius - and under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the 8.05 because the recomputed fare counts only on-optimal-route gantries. It is itemised for transparency and must never be added on top. The SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' line is different: the nearest trace fix is 834.18 m, outside the 250 m radius, so the trace never passes that gantry. POL-RD-09(4) makes that a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone SGD 1.00 correction available whether or not a deviation exists. POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged, because the only unmatched charge line is the one refunded under that limb.

6) No repeat-deviation uplift and no conduct referral. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610 (EV-DPROF-09113), so no POL-RD-06 pattern is established; there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) referral. Rating, lifetime trips, acceptance rate, prior counters and the rider's prior_no_show_flags / prior_disputes_filed / prior_disputes_upheld are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were given no weight against either party.

7) No escalation. Trip ids match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown; timestamps are consistent and run forward; the trace is sound; the advisory is present and covers the window; the refund is far below SGD 150.00; and the single unmatched line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4). The confidence floor is not approached - every artifact the ruling rests on carries weight 1.0.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.05 to the rider - SGD 8.05 under POL-RD-02 plus the SGD 1.00 POL-RD-09(4) billing correction - with a billing-integrity referral attached.

ledger.claim: The governing distance measurement is the trace, not the receipt's rounded copy: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events is 18.0 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 8.0 km or 80% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%) and clears the 50% limb as well, which is why the derived deviation status is 'material'. The trip record's own 18.0 km agrees with the trace figure, so the trace-governs sentence in POL-RD-01 raises no conflict here and no discount for a rounded convenience copy is available to the driver.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on cited artifacts: the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip id TRP-09113, and the trace's first fix at 2026-09-20T18:20:00 matches the trip record's started_at and the fare breakdown's trip window. The excess is measured from an unimpaired trace that the admissibility pre-pass assessed COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with zero gaps, so limb (b) is satisfied directly and no independent source is needed. The rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 never engages. The burden has therefore shifted to the driver to name a specific artifact and clause.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the driver cannot route this case to a 'no corroboration' outcome: POL-RD-07 limb (a) requires a gap over 90 seconds between consecutive fixes, limb (b) a straight-line jump over 500 m, limb (c) a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace has 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the limbs fires, so the deviation stands on the trace alone.

Even taking the driver's closure defence at its highest under POL-RD-03, the exoneration is capped and the cap bites hard. The advisory ADV-20260920-113 is a CLOSURE on the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, active 18:14 to 18:55 and overlapping the trip window 18:20 to 18:54, and the booked optimal route is recorded as running via that same named segment, so limb (a) and limb (b) are met. But the justified excess is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00), which is min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = min(8.0, 3.60) = 3.60 km. At most 3.60 km of the 8.0 km excess is exonerated. The remaining 4.40 km is beyond the cap, is not exonerated on any reading, and is refundable under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route.

The closure-adjusted optimal route that POL-RD-03 requires is 13.60 km: booked optimal 10.0 km plus the justified excess of 3.60 km. Its duration is the booked 20.0 minutes scaled by the ratio of adjusted to booked distance, 20.0 x (13.60 / 10.0) = 27.2 minutes. The off-route ERP must not be counted twice. The Industrial loop exit gantry charged at SGD 2.80 is flagged on_optimal_route false and its nearest trace fix is 223.17 m, so it is a genuine crossing on the deviating stretch; under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the SGD 8.05 recomputation, because the recomputed fare includes only the on-optimal-route Pelton line. It should be itemised in the ruling for transparency and must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

ledger.claim: This case should be ruled, not escalated. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires: the trip identifiers on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown all read TRP-09113; the trace is unimpaired so trigger (3) is out; the pickup time 18:20:00 is consistent across artifacts and no timestamp runs backwards; the exculpatory clause the driver relies on, POL-RD-03, is supported by an advisory actually present in the pool and covering the trip window; the computed refund is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total; the evidence is not evenly balanced, because the driver's best case is capped at 3.60 km against a measured 8.0 km; and the only unmatched charge line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. A monetary ruling should issue.

NO_ACTION is party-relative and on this record would leave the rider carrying the whole unjustified excess. The rider filed this dispute, the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so declining to act would simply preserve the SGD 8.05 the rider is contesting. What the evidence supports is the return of that contested amount as a PARTIAL_REFUND, with the SGD 1.00 billing-integrity correction standing independently alongside it.

The LTA advisory ADV-20260920-113 on EV-ADVIS-09113-01 is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE of the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, active 18:14-18:55 on 2026-09-20, which brackets the 18:20-18:54 trip window with the 15-minute buffer at each end. The platform's own optimal route runs through that very segment - the trip record's optimal_route_source reads 'routing-engine-v3.2 snapshot 2026-09-20 18:12 SGT via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory' - so limbs (a) and (b) of POL-RD-03 are met. Limb (c) is met too: the driver reported at 18:22:40 that the closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, the fare_breakdown charges the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry at 18:42, and the trace shows a route that left the Pelton Canal Link corridor and rejoined it past the closed segment. The closure does not merely 'explain' this diversion; it exonerates the driving it forced.

That exoneration is capped, and the cap on this trip is 3.60 km: min(measured excess 8.0 km, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km 12.0 - optimal_distance_km 10.0) + 1.00) = min(8.0, 3.60). The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 10.0 + 3.60 = 13.60 km, and its derived duration is optimal_duration_min 20.0 scaled by (13.60 / 10.0) = 27.2 minutes, rounded to one decimal place; amended_optimal_duration_min is null on EV-TRIP-09113, so the scaled figure governs and no substitute may be invented. Every downstream number - the POL-RD-01 establishment test and the POL-RD-02 recomputation alike - has to be run on 13.60 km and 27.2 minutes, not on the booked 10.0 km and 20.0 minutes.

The departure from the optimal corridor was rider-directed, not the driver's unilateral choice. At 18:22:40 the driver told the rider the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop; at 18:23:10 the rider answered 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion.' That is a rider instruction under POL-RD-04(a), and it falls within limb (b): the diversion entry gantry is not charged until 18:29, so the instruction precedes the corridor exit. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so I do not pretend the waypoint limb of (c) can be run; the clause's alternative limb - that the vehicle travels the requested road - is satisfied, because the fare_breakdown charges the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry and the trace comes within 223.17 m of it, placing the vehicle on the industrial loop the rider authorised. The excess attributable to that rider-directed diversion is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

On the arithmetic the driver's exposure is bounded, and the ruling must not exceed it. Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal, with the surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown (surge_multiplier 1.0 on EV-FARE-09113): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 of ERP on the optimal route = 23.416; charged_total is 31.42; refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 8.05. Run the identical arithmetic on the booked 10.0 km / 20.0 min baseline and the refund would be 12.75 - which would charge this driver for the very closure POL-RD-03 excuses him for. The lower figure is the correct one, and it is the ceiling.

The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry, which carries on_optimal_route false on EV-FARE-09113, must not be refunded twice. POL-RD-09(1) makes off-route ERP already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, precisely because the recomputed fare counts only gantries lying on the optimal route - here the Pelton lawful diversion entry at 1.00. The off-route line may be itemised in the ruling for transparency, but adding it on top of the POL-RD-02 figure would pay the same 2.80 a second time.

No billing-integrity refund arises on that off-route line either. The 'Industrial loop exit' gantry at 1.338, 103.897 is matched to the trace: the nearest fix is 223.17 m away, inside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) prescribes, so the line records a crossing the vehicle actually made and is not a phantom charge against a gantry the trace never passes.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so no uplift and no referral follows. POL-RD-06's test runs on two fields only, and both are clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 610, so neither limb - 3 or more flags, or a flag rate of 0.05 or more over at least 40 completed trips - is met. No FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is available, and POL-GEN-01 confines the test to those trailing-window counters.

After the POL-RD-03 adjustment the excess remaining is 4.4 km (18.0 - 13.60). That is 32.4% of the 13.60 km adjusted optimal and below the 8.0 km absolute mark, so the deviation is established but not MATERIAL under POL-RD-01; and even measured against the unadjusted 10.0 km baseline it is 44%, still under the 50% materiality line. The material limb of POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged on this trip, and the most this record supports is a POL-RD-02 partial refund, never a full one.
